To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Aurora-C, a kinase that complements Aurora-B in mitosis, is present in a CPC-like complex with Survivin, INCENP and Aurora-B in vivo and that Aurora-C overexpression affects CPC structure and function in cancer cells.
Aurora-C is a functional component of the CPC and is activated by phosphorylation of Survivivin on Serine 17.
Aurora-C is expressed at low levels but can complement Aurora-B in the CPC in vivo and is activated by Survivin phosphorylated on Serine 10.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the functional role of Aurora-C in human cancer and its interaction with members of the CPC.
understanding the role of Aurora-C in mitosis and its contribution to chromosomal instability and tumorigenic transformation of human cancer cells.
understanding the role of Aurora-C in the CPC and how it affects the function of the CPC in mitosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Aurora-C is a catalytic component in the CPC and its expression is regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
Aurora-C is a catalytic component and an important player in the CPC.
Aurora-C is a catalytic member of the Chromosome passenger protein complex and is a functional component of the complex in mitosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Aurora-C kinase is an important component of the Chromosome passenger complex and is involved in mitotic progression and cell cycle control through phosphorylation of the CPC components and its substrates.
Aurora-C is a catalytic subunit of the Aurora-B complex that functions in a manner that is similar to, yet distinct from Aurora-B.
Aurora-C, a minor component of the CPC in somatic cells can function as a catalytic partner of Aurora-B in mitosis and its elevated expression in cancer cells alters CPC function and structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Aurora-C is not a mere passenger protein but a functional member of the CPC.
Aurora-C is an integral component of the CPC in mitosis and its overexpression alters the structure and function of the CPC in human cancer cells.
Aurora-C is a functional component of the Chromosome passenger complex (CPC) that can be regulated independently of Aurora-B in mitosis.
